info.title: ito
info.description:
HTTP API of the Ito controller.

All request and response bodies use JSON. Request bodies are limited to 64 KiB, and unknown fields are ignored.

## Authentication

### Browser sessions

Browsers initiate sign-in via `GET /api/v1/auth/login`, which redirects to the configured OpenID Connect provider. After authentication, the provider redirects back to `GET /api/v1/auth/callback`. The callback sets the session cookie (`__Host-ito_session`, or `ito_session` when `cookie_secure` is `false`) and redirects to `/`.

The callback also sets the session's CSRF token in the readable cookie `__Host-ito_csrf` (`ito_csrf` when `cookie_secure` is `false`). The same token is returned by `GET /api/v1/session`. Every state-changing request (any method other than `GET` and `HEAD`) must include:

- `X-CSRF-Token`: the session's CSRF token
- `Origin`: the controller's configured `public_url`

An HTTP `401` response indicates that the session has expired or exceeded `session_idle`. Operations marked with the `admin` role require a session whose OIDC ID token included at least one group listed in `oidc.admin_groups` at sign-in.

### Device agents

Device agents authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer itoa_<secret>` using the bearer token returned when the device was claimed. The controller returns `401` if the agent credential has been revoked or replaced, if the device is blocked or deleting, or if the owning account is inactive.

## Concurrency control and revisions

Stateful resources include a numeric `revision` field and return it in the `ETag` header (for example, `"4"`). Update requests must send that ETag back in the `If-Match` header:

- Missing `If-Match` returns `428 Precondition Required`.
- Stale `If-Match` returns `412 Precondition Failed`.

Administrative and revocation endpoints (`POST /devices/{id}/block`, `POST /devices/{id}/unblock`, `POST /devices/{id}/revoke`, and `DELETE /devices/{id}`) accept `If-Match` optionally so concurrent updates from an agent cannot delay revocation or deletion.

When a device update commits, the background reconciler applies the desired state to the Linux kernel:

- `applied_revision` matches `revision` once the reconciler has applied and verified that revision in the kernel.
- `apply_error` contains the failure reason if the latest reconciliation pass failed.
- `disabled_reason` indicates why a device's peer is currently excluded from the kernel (such as `paused`, `outside_pools`, or `key_expired`), or `null` when the peer is enabled.

## Error responses

Errors use RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`):

```json
{
  "type": "/api/v1/problems/pool_exhausted",
  "title": "No free block of the requested size.",
  "status": 409,
  "code": "pool_exhausted",
  "instance": "urn:uuid:…",
  "detail": "…"
}
```

Clients should branch on `code`. The `Problem` schema lists all error codes with their HTTP status and title. `detail`, when present, describes the specific validation or conflict failure for the request, and `instance` contains the request UUID (also returned in the `x-request-id` header and recorded in the server logs). Internal server errors omit `detail` and record the cause in the server logs only.

When a browser navigation request sends `Accept: text/html` first, the server renders the web application's error page with the same HTTP status code instead of returning raw JSON.

## Device keys and agent login

A device record persists until deleted, while its WireGuard public key expires `key_lifetime` after it was last set. Within 60 seconds after a key expires, the reconciler removes the peer from the kernel until a key is set or renewed. Keys can be managed either from the browser or through `ito-agent`.

### Browser-managed keys

The browser generates a WireGuard key pair locally, registers the public key with `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/key` (or sends `{}` to renew the current key), and fetches `GET /api/v1/devices/{id}/config` to assemble a downloadable `wg-quick` configuration file with the local private key.

### Agent login and key rotation

An agent obtains its credential through an interactive browser approval flow:

1. The agent generates a WireGuard key pair and a 32-byte random secret encoded as unpadded base64url. It computes the request ID as the lowercase hex SHA-256 digest of the secret and opens `PUBLIC_URL/connect?id=<id>&t=<unix_seconds>` in the user's browser.
2. Within 15 minutes of `t`, the signed-in user approves the request for a specific device via `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/claims`.
3. The agent polls `POST /api/v1/agent/claim` with its secret and WireGuard public key. The server returns `202 Accepted` until the request is approved, and then returns `200 OK` with the device view and a new bearer token (`itoa_<secret>`), binding the agent's public key to the device.
4. The agent polls `GET /api/v1/agent/config` until `"ready": true` and configures the local WireGuard interface.
5. Within 3 days of `key_expires_at`, the agent renews or rotates its WireGuard key via `POST /api/v1/agent/key`.

Pending claim approvals are held in memory for 10 minutes, up to 5 concurrent approvals per account. Repeating `POST /api/v1/agent/claim` within 2 minutes of the initial claim issues a replacement credential so an agent can recover from a dropped response.

Each device has at most one active agent credential; claiming a device replaces any previous credential. A key held by any other device is refused with `key_conflict`, even within the same account. To reuse it, first revoke or delete that device, or give it a different key.

put.summary: Set a device's extra server-side routes
put.description:
Adds prefixes to the peer's `AllowedIPs` on the server interface without changing the device's
pool grants. A prefix that another device on the same interface already routes, or one inside a
pool that overlaps another device's grants, is rejected. Extra routes of different devices may
nest; WireGuard sends the overlap to the longer prefix.

Account.description: User account created on first OpenID Connect sign-in.

subject.description: OpenID Connect `sub` claim identifying the user at the provider.

idp_checked_at.description: When the account's IdP status was last applied, at sign-in or by the SCIM sweep.

idp_check_error.description: Whether the most recent SCIM user status check failed.

quota_ipv4.description: Per-account IPv4 quota override, or empty to use `quota.ipv4`.

quota_ipv6.description: Per-account IPv6 quota override, or empty to use `quota.ipv6`.

usage.description: Number of addresses currently in use per IP family, formatted as decimal strings.

AccountView.description: Account record combined with its effective quota limits and current address usage.

Addresses.description:
A device's interface addresses and routed prefix grants.

Every grant and interface address must belong to a pool on the device's interface, satisfy the
pool's `min_prefix_length`, `max_prefixes`, and `exclusions`, and avoid overlapping any server
interface address or another device's grants. The account's total usage across all devices must
stay within its quota, though shrinking an existing allocation is always allowed.

addresses.description:
Single IP addresses assigned to the client's WireGuard interface, such as `10.0.0.2`. Each
address also becomes a `/32` or `/128` grant unless it is already covered by `grants`. When
both `addresses` and `allocate_addresses` are empty, the server allocates one free address
per address family that has available pool space and quota.

allocate_addresses.description: Pool prefixes from which to allocate one additional free client address each.

grants.description: Additional prefixes routed to the device, such as `10.0.0.8/29`.

allocate_grants.description: Prefix blocks to allocate from pools as additional grants.

Allocation.description: Request to allocate one free block of `prefix_length` from a pool.

AllowedIps.description: Extra server-side routes for a device.

AuditEntry.description: Audit log entry recording a state change.

actor.description: Principal that performed the action (`account:ID`, `device:ID`, or `identity`).

Claim.description: Request body for claiming a device after interactive approval.

secret.description:
Agent secret (32 random bytes encoded as unpadded base64url) whose SHA-256 hex digest
matches the approved request ID.

public_key.description: Agent's WireGuard public key in standard base64.

device_id.description:
Expected device ID when the agent requested a specific device (`ito-agent login --device`).
If the request was approved for a different device, the claim fails with
`claim_device_mismatch` without modifying the approved device.

ClaimApproval.description: Request body for approving an agent claim on a device.

id.description: Lowercase 64-character hex SHA-256 digest of the agent's claim secret.

t.description:
Unix timestamp in seconds when the agent generated the login request (must be within the
last 15 minutes).

Claimed.description: Claimed device and newly issued agent bearer token.

token.description: Bearer token (`itoa_<secret>`) for authenticating subsequent agent requests.

Code.description: Machine-readable error code returned in API error responses.

oneOf.description: Reason the device's peer is excluded from the kernel, or `null` when enabled.

Device.description: Device record combined with the reason it is currently disabled, if any.

DeviceConfig.description: Parameters required by a client or agent to assemble its local WireGuard configuration.

enabled.description: Whether the device is currently permitted to connect.

oneOf.description: Reason the device cannot connect right now, or `null` when enabled.

ready.description:
Whether the kernel reconciler has applied the device's current revision and interface
settings without error.

addresses.description: Single IP addresses assigned to the client's WireGuard interface.

grants.description: Prefixes routed to this device on the server.

preshared_key.description: Preshared key in base64, or empty when none is configured.

route_profiles.description:
Route profiles available on the interface. When the interface defines no profiles, the
server synthesizes a single `pools` profile covering the interface's address pools.

dns_search.description:
DNS search domains, consisting of the interface's `dns_search` list followed by its
`dns_zone`.

mtu.description: Suggested client MTU, or `0` for automatic selection.

key_expires_at.description: Timestamp when the current WireGuard key expires unless renewed or rotated.

agent_credential_issued_at.description: Timestamp when the device's current agent credential was issued, or `null` if none exists.

public_key.description: New public key, or omitted to renew the existing key.

DeviceRecord.description: WireGuard peer belonging to an account on a single interface.

dns_name.description: Optional label for the device in the interface's DNS zone.

grants.description: CIDR prefixes allocated to this device from the interface's pools.

client_addresses.description: IP addresses assigned to the client's WireGuard interface.

extra_allowed_ips.description: Additional server-side AllowedIPs prefixes configured by an administrator.

blocked.description:
Whether an administrator blocked the device. Blocked devices keep their key and address
grants, but their peer is removed from the kernel, their agent credential cannot
authenticate, and non-admin owners cannot modify or delete them.

deleting.description:
Whether the device is marked for deletion and waiting for the reconciler to remove its
peer from the kernel.

applied_revision.description: Latest device revision that the reconciler applied to and verified in the kernel.

applied_enabled.description: Whether the peer is currently installed on the kernel interface.

apply_error.description:
Error from the latest reconciliation pass, or empty when applied. Set to
`interface NAME failed to apply` when interface-level setup failed.

DeviceStatus.description: Live kernel state of a device's WireGuard peer at request time.

Diagnostic.description: Live kernel state and reconciliation error for a single WireGuard interface.

oneOf.description: Observed kernel link and peers, or `null` if the interface is absent or could not be read.

DisabledReason.description: Reason a device's peer is excluded from the kernel WireGuard interface, ordered by precedence.

IdpStatus.description: Account status at the identity provider, updated on sign-in or via SCIM polling.

name.description: Linux interface name and API identifier.

applied.description: Whether the configured state has been applied to and verified in the kernel.

apply_error.description:
Error from the latest reconciliation pass, or empty when applied or when viewed by a
non-administrator.

Interface.description: Configured WireGuard interface combined with its server public key and reconciliation status.

InterfaceSettings.description: WireGuard interface configuration, address pools, and client configuration hints.

listen_port.description: UDP port the server interface listens on.

endpoint.description: External `host:port` endpoint that clients connect to.

addresses.description: CIDR addresses assigned to the server interface, such as `10.0.0.1/24`.

disabled.description: When `true`, the reconciler brings the interface down and removes all peers.

client_mtu.description: Suggested MTU for client configs, or `0` to let the client choose automatically.

dns.description: DNS server IP addresses included in client configs.

dns_search.description: DNS search domains included in client configs.

dns_zone.description:
Authoritative DNS zone served by `[dns]` for devices on this interface, or empty to disable.
Multiple interfaces can share a zone. Also appended to the client's DNS search domains after
`dns_search`.

keepalive.description: PersistentKeepalive interval in seconds for client configs, or `0` to disable.

default_profile_id.description: ID of the default route profile for clients, or empty when `route_profiles` is empty.

route_profiles.description: Named sets of client-side `AllowedIPs` that users can choose between.

pools.description: Address pools from which device addresses and prefix grants are allocated.

Link.description: Observed state of a kernel WireGuard interface.

LogoutView.description: Navigation after ending the local browser session.

redirect_url.description: Provider logout confirmation URL, or `/` if unsupported or unavailable.

account_id.description:
Owning account ID. Only administrators may specify another account; defaults to the
signed-in user's account.

dns_name.description: Optional single-label DNS name to publish in the interface's `dns_zone`.

NewDevice.description: Parameters for creating a new device.

Peer.description: Observed state of a WireGuard peer in the kernel.

handshake.description: Timestamp of the latest completed WireGuard handshake, if any.

Policy.description: Administrative policy settings for an account.

blocked.description:
Whether the account is blocked. Blocking an account immediately terminates its browser
sessions and revokes its devices.

quota.description: Per-account address limits. Empty strings inherit the installation defaults from `[quota]`.

Pool.description: Address pool from which device addresses and routed prefixes are allocated.

prefix.description:
CIDR prefix of the pool, such as `10.0.0.0/24`. Pools must not overlap within or across
interfaces.

min_prefix_length.description:
Minimum prefix length (largest block size) a single grant from this pool may have. When
unset, only single-host grants (`/32` or `/128`) are allowed.

max_prefixes.description: Maximum number of grants a single device may hold from this pool.

exclusions.description: Sub-prefixes inside the pool that are reserved and never allocated to devices.

Problem.description:
An error response, as RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`).

`code` is one of the codes in the table below; `type` is a page documenting it.

| Code | Status | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_request` | 400 | Malformed or out-of-range input. |
| `invalid_credentials` | 401 | Missing, expired or revoked session or agent credential. |
| `invalid_login` | 401 | The sign-in did not complete. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | Not allowed, or a missing or wrong CSRF token or Origin. |
| `outside_pool` | 403 | A grant lies outside every pool of the interface. |
| `identity_mapping_invalid` | 403 | The user status fetch does not know the signed-in subject. |
| `not_found` | 404 | No such resource, or not yours. |
| `method_not_allowed` | 405 | The resource does not support this method. |
| `request_timeout` | 408 | The request took too long. |
| `conflict` | 409 | A unique value is already taken. |
| `address_conflict` | 409 | An address or route is already assigned elsewhere. |
| `address_quota_exceeded` | 409 | The account's address quota would be exceeded. |
| `pool_exhausted` | 409 | No free block of the requested size. |
| `key_conflict` | 409 | The key belongs to a server or another device, or this device is blocked. |
| `dns_name_taken` | 409 | Another device publishes that name. |
| `self_block_forbidden` | 409 | Administrators cannot block themselves. |
| `claim_limit_reached` | 409 | The account has the most agent approvals pending; wait for them to be claimed or expire. |
| `claim_taken` | 409 | Another account approved this agent request. |
| `claim_device_mismatch` | 409 | The request was approved for a device other than the one the agent asks for. |
| `revision_conflict` | 412 | If-Match is stale. |
| `request_too_large` | 413 | The body is over 64 KiB. |
| `unsupported_media_type` | 415 | The body is not application/json. |
| `precondition_required` | 428 | If-Match is missing. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | A bug; the log has the cause. |
| `identity_unavailable` | 503 | The identity provider did not answer as expected. |
| `secret_unavailable` | 503 | A configured secret file cannot be read. |
| `kernel_unavailable` | 503 | An ip or wg command could not run. |
| `kernel_command_failed` | 503 | An ip or wg command failed. |
| `interface_ownership_mismatch` | 503 | The interface name belongs to a link the controller does not own. |
| `interface_name_in_use` | 503 | The interface name belongs to a link that is not WireGuard. |
| `database_unavailable` | 503 | The database did not answer. |

type.description: Problem type URI (`/api/v1/problems/CODE`) documenting the error code.

title.description: Short human-readable summary for this error code.

detail.description: Specific explanation of what failed in this request, when applicable.

instance.description: Request occurrence URI (`urn:uuid:REQUEST-ID`), matching `x-request-id` and server logs.

Psk.description: Preshared key update request; specify either `generate: true` or `preshared_key`.

preshared_key.description: Base64 preshared key, or empty to clear it.

generate.description: Whether the server should generate a random preshared key.

Quota.description:
Address limits per IP family, expressed as a decimal address count or a prefix length such as
`/64`.

RouteProfile.description:
Named set of `AllowedIPs` that a client can select for its local tunnel routes. Selecting a
profile changes only the client's `AllowedIPs`, leaving the server's peer routes unchanged.

id.description: Profile identifier: a DNS label that is unique within the interface.

name.description: Display name shown to users in the portal and agent UI.

allowed_ips.description: Client-side `AllowedIPs` prefixes routed through the tunnel when this profile is active.

admin.description:
Whether the session has administrator privileges, as determined by `oidc.admin_groups` at
sign-in.

csrf_token.description:
CSRF token for the session, also set in the `__Host-ito_csrf` cookie. Must be sent in the
`X-CSRF-Token` header on every request other than `GET` and `HEAD`.

Settings.description: Mutable device settings; omitted fields remain unchanged.

dns_name.description: DNS label for the device in its interface's zone, or empty to opt out of DNS publication.

agent.description: Device agent credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer itoa_SECRET`.

csrf.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrf.description: CSRF token read from the `__Host-ito_csrf` cookie and sent in the `X-CSRF-Token` header on mutating requests.

session.name: __Host-ito_session
session.description: Browser session secret sent in the `__Host-ito_session` cookie (`ito_session` when `cookie_secure = false`).

tags.description: Configured WireGuard interfaces, address pools, server public keys, and kernel reconciliation state.
